2027-03-18.title: Thursday of the Fifth Week of Lent
readings: You shall be the ancestor of a multitude of nations
The Lord remembers his covenant for ever
Your ancestor Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day
2027-03-18.alt: Lenten weekday of the fifth week. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. From the Fifth Sunday of Lent crosses and images may be veiled until the Passion is celebrated (where the bishops' conference allows). Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Cyril of Jerusalem, bishop and Doctor of the Church (its collect may be used).
2027-03-18.verse: Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
theo: Abram is ninety-nine years old and childless when God appears to him again. He falls on his face, and God speaks: “As for me, this is my covenant with you: You shall be the ancestor of a multitude of nations. No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham.” A new name means a new mission. God binds himself with an everlasting covenant, “to be God to you and to your offspring after you,” and asks Abraham to keep it, he and his descendants. The whole history of Israel hangs on this promise, and so does ours: St Paul will say that all who belong to Christ are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise (Galatians 3:29). The Psalm answers with wonder that God never forgets: “He is mindful of his covenant forever, of the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations.” In the last days of Lent, as the elect prepare for Baptism, the Church reminds us that God's covenant is older and stronger than our failures.

In the Gospel the argument about Abraham reaches its peak. Jesus says: “whoever keeps my word will never see death.” His hearers object that Abraham died, and the prophets died: “Who do you claim to be?” Jesus answers that Abraham “rejoiced that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad.” They reply, “You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?” Then comes the most daring sentence in the Gospel: “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.” He does not say I was, but I AM, the name of God revealed to Moses. Some take up stones, judging it blasphemy, and Jesus slips away from the Temple. When John writes “the Jews” in such scenes, he usually means the leaders and opponents in Jerusalem, not the whole Jewish people, of whom Jesus, Mary and the apostles were members; the Church firmly rejects any use of these texts to blame the Jewish people (Nostra Aetate 4). Today we remember St Cyril of Jerusalem (about 313 to 386), bishop of the city where these words were spoken. Around the year 350 he gave his famous Catechetical Lectures to those preparing for Easter Baptism, near the place of the Cross and the empty tomb, and after Easter he explained to the newly baptized the mysteries they had received. Exiled three times in the struggles against the Arian heresy, he held fast to the faith that Jesus is truly God, the I AM before Abraham.
outline: Ask: what does your name mean, and who gave it to you?
A new name and an everlasting covenant.
The promise looks forward to Christ.
Point 3 · Before Abraham was, I am
Jesus, the eternal Son; St Cyril, teacher of the faith.
live: Thank God today for your Baptism, the day you entered his covenant; find out its date if you do not know it.
Choose one word of Jesus from this week's Gospels and live it today.
2027-03-18.prayer: God of Abraham, you never forget your covenant. Thank you for making us, in Christ, heirs of your promise. Lord Jesus, before Abraham was, you are; we adore you as true God and true man. Through the prayers of St Cyril of Jerusalem, who taught the faith to the newly baptized, keep us faithful to our Baptism and lead the elect safely to Easter. Amen.
altar: St Cyril taught the newly baptized (in substance): do not regard the bread and wine as plain bread and wine, for they are the Body and Blood of Christ as the Lord declared; let faith assure you. At every Mass the eternal I AM gives himself to us.

quick: God made an everlasting covenant with Abraham and gave him a new name.
Jesus says that Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and that before Abraham was, I AM.
St Cyril of Jerusalem taught the catechumens and defended the divinity of Christ.
2027-03-18.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-03-18.question: Do I believe, with all my heart, that Jesus is God, the I AM before Abraham?

family.explain: God made a special promise to Abram: you will be the father of many nations! And God gave him a new name, Abraham. God promised to be his God and the God of his children for ever. Jesus said: before Abraham was born, I AM. Jesus is God, who was there before everything.
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we baptized? Shall we look for the date and celebrate it this year?”

illus: In a village parish near Kollam the catechism teacher had the children bring their baptism certificates to class. One girl discovered she had been baptized on the same date as her grandmother, sixty years apart. The old woman cried when she heard it and said: God has kept his promise for three generations in our family. The class wrote the dates on a chart and promised to pray for each other on their baptism days.

pm.open: God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, you remember your covenant for ever. Lord Jesus, before Abraham was, you are. We adore you. Amen.
share: No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham (Genesis 17:5). What new name, what mission, has God given me?
Whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). How do I keep the word of Jesus?
Before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). Do I worship Jesus as God?
pm.resp: The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
interc: For the elect and catechumens preparing for Easter Baptism, through the prayers of St Cyril.
For catechists and teachers of the faith, that they may teach with clarity and love.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in love of his name and faithfulness to his covenant.
For Christians in Jerusalem and the Holy Land, especially as Holy Week approaches.
For our group, that we may live our baptismal promises.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to your covenant for a thousand generations. Make us faithful children of Abraham in Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abram is ninety-nine years old and has no son, and God says: you shall be the ancestor of a multitude of nations. No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham (Genesis 17:4–5). A new name means a new mission. God makes an everlasting covenant, and he never forgets it.

In the Gospel Jesus says: your ancestor Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad (John 8:56). All the promises to Abraham were looking forward to Jesus. In him the blessing reaches all nations, and we too become Abraham's children by faith and Baptism.

Then Jesus says: very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). Not I was, but I AM, the holy name of God. This is why some picked up stones. Jesus is not only a great teacher. He is the eternal Son of God, who was before Abraham and before the world.

St Cyril of Jerusalem, whom we remember today, taught this faith to those preparing for Baptism near the very place of the Cross and the empty tomb, and suffered exile to defend it. Let us renew our own baptismal faith as Easter approaches, and adore Jesus, true God and true man. Amen.
kids: Children, God gave Abram a new name, Abraham, and promised him a family as big as the stars. Jesus said something amazing: before Abraham was born, I AM. Jesus was always there, because he is God! Ask your parents today the date of your Baptism, the day you joined God's family.

intro: The covenant with Abraham, the joy of seeing Christ's day, and the eternal Son; St Cyril of Jerusalem.

sub: A new name, a new mission.
q: No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you the ancestor of a multitude of nations.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises in your own words tonight before you sleep.

sub: He remembers for a thousand generations.
q: I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your offspring after you throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.
Thus he has shown the mercy promised to our ancestors, and has remembered his holy covenant, the oath that he swore to our ancestor Abraham,
points.apply: Pray the Benedictus (Luke 1:68–79) in the morning this week, thanking God who keeps his covenant.

sub: Not I was, but I AM.
The stones and the hidden Lord.
Cyril's faith in the divinity of Christ.
q: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever you had formed the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
points.apply: Make a slow genuflection before the tabernacle each time you enter church this week, adoring the I AM.

concl: God's covenant with Abraham is everlasting, and in Christ we are its heirs.
Jesus is the eternal Son, the I AM, whom St Cyril taught and defended.
2027-03-18.resolve: Find the date of your Baptism and keep it this year as a day of thanksgiving.
